header.title: Site rules
header.description: Which release pages rDownloader recognises, and by which rule. No rule arrives with the program: import the signed rule file every release carries, or write your own. Every rule here is yours to switch, edit, duplicate and remove.

list.title: Rules
list.empty: No rule is installed, so no release page is recognised by rule. Import the signed rule file of a release to start from the project's rules.
list.group_off: The group is switched off, so this rule is not consulted.

editor.description: Every field is a field, not a line of JSON. Try the rule against a real address before you save it.
editor.id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It cannot be changed later and never repeats another rule's.
editor.name: Name
editor.group_hint: What the list groups and the group switch covers.
editor.version_hint: Raise it when you change the rule.
editor.hosts_hint: One per line. `*.example.org` covers everything below the host; the first entry must be a concrete host.
editor.paths_hint: One regular expression per line, over the path with its query. Empty claims every path.
editor.dead_hint: One per line. An address on one of them is rewritten to the first host above.
editor.probe_hint: A real page this rule claims. The self-test fetches it.
editor.mirrors: The links are copies of one file
editor.mirrors_hint: True for a release page that posts one file to several hosters.
editor.incomplete: Identifier, name, group, one host, one step and a probe address are needed.

steps.heading: Steps
steps.description: They run in this order. `fetch` writes the page into `page`; the links are whatever ends up in `links`.
steps.url_hint: Empty means the address the run was given. `${name}` inserts a variable.
steps.empty: A rule needs at least one step.

test.heading: Trial run
test.description: Give a real address this rule claims. Nothing is saved by the run.
test.package_none: The rule found no package name.
test.mirrors: The rule declares these links to be copies of one file.

verdicts.claimed: A resolver or backend speaks for it
verdicts.not-a-file: Answers with a page, not a file

transfer.heading: Carry rules
transfer.export_empty: There is no rule to export.
transfer.import_hint: Takes the signed rule file of a release or a rule export. Every imported rule arrives switched off, signed or not. Try it, then switch it on yourself.
transfer.import_unreadable: That file is neither the signed rule file nor a rule export.
transfer.imported: {stored} of {total} rules were stored, switched off.
transfer.imported_signed: The signed rule file verified: {stored} of {total} rules were stored, switched off.

delete.title: Remove this rule?
delete.description: {name} is removed from this installation. Export it first if you want to keep it.

duplicate_hint: Makes a switched-off copy under a new identifier and opens it in the editor
duplicated: {name} was created, switched off, and opened for editing.
